# Draft:Chronicles of Constitutional Movements in Nineteenth-Century Europe

Chronicles of Constitutional Movements in Nineteenth-Century Europe is a historical work by Hungarian author Anett Győri, focusing on European constitutional movements in the 19th century. The book was first published on September 9, 2024, in London by Lambert Academic Publishing, and was subsequently promoted internationally by Omniscriptum Publishers. Since its release, the book has garnered attention at several international book fairs. The book is available on multiple global platforms and other major booksellers, attesting to the book's international reach.
Overview
The book examines the constitutional movements of the 19th century, analyzing their historical significance and key events across Europe. It includes contemporary images and cartoons that help illustrate the period's developments. The central focus of the work is the causes of the Hungarian Revolution of 1848 and the subsequent uprisings, offering a detailed analysis of these events within the broader context of European history.
The author adopts a chronological approach to the events leading up to the Hungarian Revolution, exploring the political and legal context of Europe following the French Revolution. Through primary sources, including those translated by the author, the study provides a comprehensive account of the period, focusing on the political struggles and constitutional challenges faced by revolutionaries and intellectuals in Germany and Hungary. The work contrasts the centralization efforts of the Habsburg monarchy with the defense of constitutional rights by the Hungarian people.
Translations
The book has been translated into multiple languages and continues to receive recognition internationally. It has made an impact at various book fairs and continues to be available in numerous countries.
